topic: The Curious Link: Block Collisions and the Digits of Pi

outline.topic: The Curious Link: Block Collisions and the Digits of Pi

sections.title: The Hook: The Bouncing Block Paradox
sections.content: Introduce the physical system: two blocks of different masses on a frictionless surface, with a wall on the left. Block A (mass m) sits between the wall and Block B (mass M). We count the number of collisions.
sections.example: A small ant (Block A) and a large elephant (Block B) sliding on ice towards a solid stone wall.

sections.title: Prerequisites: Conservation Laws
sections.content: Briefly explain that in elastic collisions, both Kinetic Energy and Momentum are conserved. Use a vector diagram to show how velocity vectors change after impact, emphasizing the velocity reflection rule.
sections.example: Visualizing the velocity vectors of the ant and elephant as arrows changing direction upon collision, represented by a reflection across an energy-conserving boundary.

sections.title: The Scaling Connection: Phase Space
sections.content: Explain that the collision system can be mapped to a billiard ball bouncing inside a circular boundary. The 'angle' of the collision represents the digits of Pi. As mass M increases by powers of 100, the collision count increases by digits of Pi.
sections.example: An animation showing a light ray bouncing inside a circle; as the mass ratio M/m grows, the 'path' of the collision count converges to 3.1415...

sections.title: Deep Dive: The 1:100 Ratio
sections.content: Demonstrate that if Block B is 100^n times heavier than Block A, the total number of collisions is exactly the first n+1 digits of Pi.
sections.example: Table graphic: 1:1 ratio = 3 collisions; 1:100 ratio = 31 collisions; 1:10,000 ratio = 314 collisions.

sections.title: Synthesis & Summary
sections.content: Summarize how a mechanical, discrete system (blocks hitting) generates a transcendental, continuous constant (Pi). Reiterate that the physics of conservation laws creates a geometric shadow of Pi.
sections.example: Final visual: A computer simulation of blocks colliding, where the collision counter progressively spells out 3.14159...

storyboard.title: The Hook: The Bouncing Block Paradox
lecture_lines: Can blocks colliding count the digits of Pi?
Two blocks bounce on a frictionless surface.
Small Block A sits near a wall.
Larger Block B blocks the path.
Total collisions reveal the digits of Pi.
animations: Create a 2D block (#FFFFFF) falling onto a surface (#4D4D4D).
Animate the block bouncing, changing color to #FF5733 at the peak.
Display a visual representation of energy loss, fading color from #FF5733 to #33FF57.

storyboard.title: Prerequisites: Conservation Laws
lecture_lines: Elastic collisions conserve momentum and kinetic energy.
Velocity reflects perfectly against stationary objects.
Energy remains trapped within the system.
animations: Label Momentum (#F1C40F) and Energy (#3498DB) on screen.
Animate a vector for momentum, showing conservation during collision.
Show energy dissipating as heat, using particles (#E74C3C) escaping the block.

storyboard.title: The Scaling Connection: Phase Space
lecture_lines: Collisions map to a billiard ball's path.
The ball bounces inside a circular boundary.
Mass ratios determine the trajectory angle.
Larger mass ratios track digits of Pi.
animations: Draw a coordinate grid, marking positions X and Y.
Animate a trajectory line (#FFFFFF) evolving through the phase space.
Highlight the convergence points with pulsating circles (#F39C12).
Animate a path segment (#BDC3C7) to illustrate phase stability.
Fade in a label for 'Phase Stability' (#FFFFFF).

storyboard.title: Deep Dive: The 1:100 Ratio
lecture_lines: Increase mass ratio by powers of 100.
Total collisions match consecutive digits of Pi.
animations: Present a ratio scale diagram showing 1 unit to 100 units.
Animate a shrinking action on the large block (#3498DB) to match the small one (#2ECC71).
Highlight the 1:100 ratio numerical label with a yellow flash (#F1C40F).
Show the dynamic scaling process repeating three times.
Fade out the scaling diagrams to show a final comparison result.

storyboard.title: Synthesis & Summary
lecture_lines: Conservation laws create geometric shadows of Pi.
Discrete impacts mirror continuous mathematical truth.
animations: Display a summary list of the key points covered.
Pulse the background (#000000) to emphasize the core paradox solution.
Final image fades in: all mechanical elements joined as a single system (#FFFFFF).
